programme: CDX2 sets intestinal/gastric epithelial identity and, together with the enteroendocrine-neurosecretory cascade INSM1 and NEUROD1, specifies hormone-producing gut epithelial cells; CRX and NR2E3, normally a photoreceptor-specific pair (they co-target NRL, RHO, PRPH2), are the terminal neurosecretory-differentiation genes that this cascade switches on ectopically when the programme is pushed to its extreme.
role_in_a: In IBS-relevant gut epithelium, CDX2 maintains intestinal identity and, via the NEUROD1/INSM1 branch, is expected to set enteroendocrine (serotonin- and peptide-secreting) cell specification — the population implicated in visceral sensitivity and motility symptoms. Retrieved support for this role is limited to CDX2 itself (Open Targets association, and a GWAS of peptic ulcer disease that names IBS among the GI disorders linked to CDX2); no retrieved record places INSM1, NEUROD1, CRX or NR2E3 in IBS.
role_in_b: In stomach cancer the same cascade runs in two documented directions: CDX2-driven intestinal metaplasia is a recognized precursor of intestinal-type gastric cancer and also acts directly on invasion/migration signaling, while INSM1 and NEUROD1 mark gastric neuroendocrine tumors and small-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, with CRX appearing among the transcriptional regulators of gastric cancer and NR2E3 scoring highly in Open Targets alongside its obligate partner CRX.
shared_axis: Both diseases sit on the same CDX2-anchored gut epithelial differentiation axis with its enteroendocrine/neurosecretory branch (INSM1, NEUROD1, CRX, NR2E3); in stomach cancer this axis is pushed to a malignant extreme (metaplasia, neuroendocrine transformation), whereas in IBS the same axis is proposed to operate within normal epithelium, where enteroendocrine cell output governs gut sensory and motor tone.
reasoning: The module is clearly nameable and four of its five carrying factors (CDX2, INSM1, NEUROD1, CRX) are independently placed in stomach cancer by retrieved papers, so the stomach-cancer half is well grounded. The IBS half rests almost entirely on one broad GWAS paper for CDX2 and on general enteroendocrine biology for the rest, not on anything retrieved for INSM1/NEUROD1/CRX/NR2E3 in IBS, so the cross-disease connection is reasoning-driven rather than record-driven.
support: 28078605 — places CRX among the transcriptional regulators identified in a gastric cancer mRNA microarray network; 40358853 — characterizes INSM1 expression in gastric neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine tumors; 38434925 — reports INSM1-relevant gastric small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma with loss of epithelial markers, evidencing the epithelial-to-neuroendocrine transition; 42205459 — shows CDX2 driving a signaling axis that regulates gastric cancer cell invasion and migration; 31614322 — links NEUROD1 to gastric cancer via miR-374a-5p regulation; 33608531 — GWAS of peptic ulcer disease placing CDX2 in relation to Helicobacter pylori-associated and other GI disorders, the only retrieved paper touching both IBS and a gastric-adjacent condition.
how_to_falsify: Quantify enteroendocrine/enterochromaffin cell density and CDX2/NEUROD1/INSM1 expression by immunohistochemistry or single-cell RNA-seq in colonic/rectal biopsies from IBS patients versus matched controls; if cell numbers and factor expression do not differ and do not track with symptom severity or mucosal serotonin, the IBS side of the account fails. On the cancer side, if CDX2-high gastric tumors and INSM1/NEUROD1/CRX-positive neuroendocrine gastric tumors do not share the predicted target-gene overlap (e.g. GCG/SST/INS-family genes), the claim that this is one coherent cascade rather than two unrelated programmes also fails.
caveats: 120 patient-group comparisons come from a single independent cohort pair, so this is one dataset examined many ways, not independent replication. The tissues compared are colorectal (IBS) and stomach (cancer), not the same organ, so the axis must hold across distinct regional epithelium. No tissue-generic exclusions were listed for this pair, so the absence of a 'master gut regulator' (e.g. HNF1A, which only topped one patient group and is listed under single-view exclusions) reflects lack of recurrence, not filtering. Several concordant factors — ATOH8, BCL11A, HOXA2, DBP, TFDP2, IKZF2, and E2F8 — were left out of the programme because they share no targets with the CDX2/neuroendocrine cascade and have no documented role in either disease in the retrieved record; including them would manufacture a mechanism the data does not support.
